KJV.name: King James Version (KJV)
KJV.description: The King James Version (KJV), commissioned in 1604 and published in 1611 by King James I of England, is a widely revered Early Modern English translation of the Christian Bible. Known for its majestic, rhythmic, and poetic style, it served as the standard English Bible for over 300 years. It was produced by 54 scholars using a formal equivalence approach, relying on the Masoretic Text for the Old Testament and the Textus Receptus for the New Testament.

ASV.name: American Standard Version (ASV)
ASV.description: The American Standard Version (ASV) of 1901 is a highly literal, word-for-word (formal equivalence) English translation of the Bible. Known as the "Standard American Edition" of the Revised Version, it was produced to incorporate the best available 19th-century scholarship and to correct the archaic language and textual basis of the King James Version (KJV). While its rigid, sometimes archaic style limited its long-term popularity, it is regarded as a foundational, highly accurate text for study.

CPDV.name: Catholic Public Domain Version (CPDV)
CPDV.description: The Catholic Public Domain Version (CPDV) is a modern English translation of the Bible based on the Sixto-Clementine Latin Vulgate, aimed at providing a freely accessible, accurate, and traditionally oriented text. Translated primarily by Ronald L. Conte Jr., it uses the Challoner Douay-Rheims version as a guide, ensuring alignment with Roman Catholic doctrine without utilizing "inclusive language".
